en.title: All Split Matches of Digit-String Codes
en.description:
You are given a digit string panel and several code strings. Split each code into index and pattern, with the index part having length 1 through len(code)-1 in order; parse index as a decimal integer (leading zeros do not affect the value). If the contiguous segment of panel starting at that 0-based index exactly equals pattern, the result of that split is pattern; otherwise it is not found. Output the results in code order, then in order of split length.

Standard input/output and this site's supplementary ranges follow this problem's description.
en.input: The first line contains panel (1..1000 ASCII digits); the second line contains c (1≤c≤100), followed by c lines, each an ASCII digit string code, with 2≤len(code)≤100 and total code characters ≤5000. The above upper bounds on c and code are site supplements that keep the output from becoming too large. Each index and pattern has at least one digit.
en.output: Output one line per split: pattern if it matches, otherwise not found. The order follows the input order of code, and within each code, increasing split length.
en.explanation: For each code, enumerate every split position where both index and pattern are non-empty, convert the left part to an integer, and compare it against the slice of panel of the same length.
